Validating final source-table records

Source: vignettes/validating.Rmd
validating.Rmd
library(dicr)

Validation checks the records after cleaning and filtering. For example, if cleaning fills in a death year and filtering removes a header row, QA should inspect the filled-in value and ignore the removed row. Run the stages in order:

fetch_source("path/to/source.yaml")
extract_source("path/to/source.yaml")
clean_source("path/to/source.yaml")
filter_source("path/to/source.yaml")
validate_source("path/to/source.yaml")

validate_source() never changes the filtered data. A passing table gets an RDS with the same rows, columns, values, and order, plus a YAML sidecar under validated/{state}/{vintage}_{years}. A failing table gets a separate failure report instead of a new validated pair.

Describe the records you expect

Add qa to a legacy single-table source-file config or to an inline source table. Suppose the final table contains Jane Doe with a recorded death year, but the source did not provide her death date:

qa:
  required_columns: [record_locator, full_name, death_year]
  expected_blanks: [death_date]
  examples:
    - record_locator: "'Deaths'!A2:D2"
      full_name: Jane Doe
      death_year: 2020
      death_date: null
  constraints:
    death_year:
      min: 2019
      max: 2024
    full_name:
      unique: true

The example checks only the fields shown for that surviving locator. Here death_date: null checks the absence of a date, while expected_blanks checks that every row lacks one. When expected_blanks is present, any all-NA column not listed there also fails validation. Without expected_blanks, all-NA columns are not checked. required_columns rejects NA; it does not treat empty strings or whitespace as missing. If Jane’s name differs from the example, the report identifies her locator without changing the record.

A constraint can also list accepted values with options: [2019, 2020], or combine options, inclusive min/max, and unique: true on one column. Missing values pass constraints unless the column is also required. A repeated nonmissing value flags every record sharing it. Text bounds and options compare exact final values without trimming or case folding. Configured dates and numbers are converted using the same schema types as filtering; pass schema_path if the schema is not in the project root.

Reuse expectations across tables

A format can declare a shared qa block. A formatted source table with no qa inherits it; a table with its own block replaces the whole block. For example, if a format requires full_name and death_year, this table checks only full_name:

source_tables:
  - source_table_id: ca_first
    format: path/to/format.yaml
    qa:
      required_columns: [full_name]

qa: {} or qa: null deliberately publishes without checks. If neither the format nor the table has a qa key, validation warns once per table on each call, even when its output is already cached. Inline tables use their own qa; a file-level qa is not inherited by multi-table configs.

Inspect the result

The returned list is keyed by effective source-table ID. Run one table with source_table_id, or omit it to try every table independently:

result <- validate_source("path/to/source.yaml", source_table_id = "ca_first")
result$ca_first$status  # "written" or "skipped" when the pair is current

The successful YAML sidecar includes effective checks, a summary for each check, input/output record counts, and config and input identity. When a check fails, the console gives a brief error and <source_id>-failures.yaml contains the full details. For instance, a missing required year is attributed to its record:

failures:
  - check: required_columns
    column: death_year
    type: records
    failure_count: 1
    record_locators: ["'Deaths'!A2:D2"]

Independent checks continue so the report includes other affected locators as well. A failure leaves any earlier successful validated RDS/YAML pair intact; a later success or valid cache hit removes the stale report. To recheck an unchanged input instead of skipping the cached result, use validate_source("path/to/source.yaml", force = TRUE). A filtered input that is not a data frame or lacks record_locator fails before QA and does not create a failure report. See Filtering for preparing the input records.
